h: Black pudding, steam trains and Sir Robert Peel
p: Bury town centre is compact and easy to get around, and Mill Gate sits right in the middle of it, so you can park up or hop off the tram and see a lot without much effort. The Metrolink runs all the way from Manchester city centre, which makes Bury an easy day out without the car.

First stop for most people is the market. Bury Market is famous across the North West, and the town is known for its black pudding, so it would be rude not to try some. Have it hot from a stall with a bit of mustard, which is a local favourite. The market hall and outdoor stalls sell everything from fresh food to clothes and household bits.

In the town square you'll see the statue of Sir Robert Peel, who was born in Bury, served as Prime Minister and set up the Metropolitan Police, which is why police officers were once nicknamed bobbies. It's a nice bit of history to point out to the kids.

Just round the corner, Bury Art Museum houses a fine collection of Victorian paintings and changing exhibitions. The Fusilier Museum tells the story of the Lancashire Fusiliers, with medals, uniforms and personal stories.

The big family favourite is the East Lancashire Railway, a heritage steam line that runs from Bolton Street Station through the Irwell valley towards Ramsbottom and Rawtenstall. Ramsbottom is a lovely little town for lunch. Need fresh air? Burrs Country Park, a short drive or walk north of the centre, has riverside paths and open space to stretch your legs.
